# case-F6 — ledger-matched file → `SAFE(moved-to-obsidian)`

Fixture for fixture case **F6** in `tools/souji-verify.spec.md`:

> F6 ledger-matched file (ledger row + matching sha256 both sides) →
> SAFE(moved-to-obsidian)

The case proves the gate is the **ledger row**, not the existence of a vault
copy: a file is SAFE only when the live ledger holds a row matching
**source path + source sha256 + vault path + vault sha256** (all four
conjuncts).

## Files

| path | role |
|---|---|
| `make-fixture.sh` | builder; creates the source repo, the fake vault, and the ledger injection payload |
| `expected.json` | declaration: the ledger rows the tool SHOULD find, the four targets, and the armed/disarmed verdicts |
| `README.md` | this contract |
| `tests/results/ledger-inject.txt` | generated by `make-fixture.sh`; the runner appends its rows to the live ledger |

`expected.json` uses the placeholder `@FIXTURE_ROOT@`; substitute the
`FIXTURE_ROOT` printed by the builder. `make-fixture.sh` also writes the
same substitution already applied to `<FIXTURE_ROOT>/ledger-inject.txt`.

## What the builder creates

```
<FIXTURE_ROOT>/
  .case-F6-fixture          marker; re-running with the same --out rebuilds the tree
  source/                   git repo (kind-3 file artifacts live here)
    README.md                   committed on `main` (the pushed baseline)
    src/heredoc-quorum-notes.md      TARGET  ledger-match
    src/not-exported-notes.md        control no ledger row
    src/hash-mismatch-notes.md       control row has the pre-edit source hash
    src/vault-drift-notes.md         control row has the pre-drift vault hash
  vault/                    fake Obsidian vault, files mode 0444
    heredoc-quorum-notes.md          byte-identical to the source (same sha256)
    not-exported-notes.md            byte-identical to the source, no row
    hash-mismatch-notes.md           pre-edit content (differs from source)
    vault-drift-notes.md             edited after export (differs from source)
  ledger-inject.txt         the 3 payload rows (tab-separated, ledger column order)
```

Git shape: the four `src/` files are committed on branch `export-prep`; the
`pushed` receipt resolves the default branch through
`refs/remotes/origin/HEAD → origin/main` (commit `36b5fc01…`) and the
introducing commit `a03ed477…` is **not** an ancestor of it. The `pushed`
receipt therefore cannot fire for any target, so `SAFE(moved-to-obsidian)` is
observable only through the ledger. `git status` is clean and all refs are
synthesized locally (`update-ref`/`symbolic-ref`); no network, no fetch.

## Consumption contract

```bash
# 1. build (default root: fresh mktemp -d; nothing else is written)
ROOT=$(bash tests/fixtures/case-F6/make-fixture.sh --quiet | sed -n 's/^FIXTURE_ROOT=//p')

# 2. arm — snapshot the live ledger, then append the payload (rows only; the
#    header must not be duplicated)
cp corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv /tmp/case-F6-ledger.bak
cat tests/results/ledger-inject.txt >> corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv

# 3. evaluate by exact absolute path
tools/souji-verify.sh "$ROOT/source/src/heredoc-quorum-notes.md" \
                      "$ROOT/source/src/not-exported-notes.md" \
                      "$ROOT/source/src/hash-mismatch-notes.md" \
                      "$ROOT/source/src/vault-drift-notes.md"

# 4. disarm — restore the pre-arm ledger
cp /tmp/case-F6-ledger.bak corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv
```

`make-fixture.sh` never writes the live ledger. `--quiet` emits only
`KEY=VALUE` lines plus one `TARGET=<id>:<path>` line per target;
`--print-injection --out DIR` prints the concrete rows without building;
`--print-hashes` prints the content sha256 table. Exit codes: 0 ok,
1 build/assertion failure, 2 usage.

## Verdict matrix (binding)

| target | armed (rows injected) | disarmed (no rows) |
|---|---|---|
| `ledger-match` | `SAFE(moved-to-obsidian)` | `NOT-SAFE` |
| `not-exported` | `NOT-SAFE` | `NOT-SAFE` |
| `source-hash-mismatch` | `NOT-SAFE` | `NOT-SAFE` |
| `vault-hash-drift` | `NOT-SAFE` | `NOT-SAFE` |

- For `ledger-match` the exact pair `SAFE` + receipt `moved-to-obsidian` is
  binding.
- For the three controls only the `NOT-SAFE` verdict is binding; the reason
  text is informational (the spec admits more than one NOT-SAFE reason).
- With the ledger disarmed every target must be `NOT-SAFE`; a `SAFE` there is
  a false positive against the ledger gate.

Each control breaks exactly one conjunct of the ledger match, so a tool that
checks only paths or only one hash fails at least one row:

| control | source path | source sha256 | vault path | vault sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ledger-match` | match | match | match | match |
| `not-exported` | — no row — | | | |
| `source-hash-mismatch` | match | **mismatch** | match | match |
| `vault-hash-drift` | match | match | match | **mismatch** |

## Determinism

Content, git identity and dates are fixed, so the fixture is reproducible:
two builds at different roots produce byte-identical trees and commit hashes
(`initial=36b5fc01…`, `export-prep=a03ed477…`). The builder asserts every
written file against the six content sha256 constants and cross-checks them
against `expected.json`; a drift is a hard failure. `--out` re-runs are safe
only on a directory carrying the `.case-F6-fixture` marker (or an empty
directory); anything else non-empty is refused rather than deleted.

## Notes for implementation seats

- Under `--selftest`, do **not** append to `corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv`.
  Build the fixture with `--out <tmpdir>` and point the ledger lookup at a
  temporary ledger: header row of the live ledger + `<tmpdir>/ledger-inject.txt`.
  A ledger-path override (e.g. `SOUJI_LEDGER`) is the expected seam.
- The `pushed` receipt must be evaluated before `moved-to-obsidian`; here it
  deterministically fails (`PUSHED_RECEIPT_PROBE=not-pushed`), which is what
  isolates the ledger gate.
- The vault is a plain directory; nothing in the fixture requires repository
  context for it. Vault files are mode 0444 — the tool must only read them.
- Row matching uses the absolute path strings in the payload; invoke the tool
  with the exact paths printed by the builder (no relative-path rewriting).
